pitch_detail.notes: Set off roughly five feet to the right of the chimney, then cut left into the central weakness. A runnel (hooking and bridging) gives access to a snow field, climb a steep loose rock bulge to a second snow field, and belay in a small alcove. The alcove belay takes a .75, #1, .3 and #3.

Leave the alcove by traversing left, then bridge and squirm upward past a chockstone. Protection is sparse; an old frayed fixed rope hangs here and should not be trusted. Past the chockstone, moderate snow and mixed ground lead to a belay in a cave.

Squirm up the chimney above the belay and past the big chockstone. Rock quality is poor with plenty of loose stuff, and whoever is belaying has little cover. Heave over the chockstone and continue to a belay at a large tree.
Rock steps and turf lead up and slightly left to a ribbon feature that traverses the face. From there many finishes are possible, including any of the established rock routes.

review.changed: 4 pitches written (stored count is 6; the text covers four). Route was climbed with no fixed protection left.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=6 but the text describes only 4. Stored grade is a combined ice and mixed string; the text rates difficulties up to 5.9+ M5.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb to a roof about 60 ft up, make some undercling moves, then follow a loose, awkward corner to the anchor in the white band of rock. The belay is two knife-blade pitons.
A short pitch following a thin black streak to the ridge, with six bolts on interesting rock and engaging moves. The climbing has a rough, mixed feel overall.

review.changed: 2 pitches; no grades or lengths per pitch in the text.

pitch_detail.notes: Face climbing to a bolted belay.
A short pitch that gets you to the base of the tower. The belay is bolted.

The crux pitch: it follows a left-facing corner all the way to the buttress top. A 4-inch cam may help here. It can also be climbed on its own by skirting the base of the upper section from the east, skipping the first two pitches.

review.changed: 3 pitches with grades and anchors. Descent is by several rappels on one 60 m rope but no station list so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Locate the bolt line (a few bolts carry homemade hangers). The first 50 ft is real climbing; above, it degrades to a ledgy ramble up to a big ledge with a two-bolt anchor. Not a great pitch, but better than hiking.
Scramble right, then up, to where the tower above begins to steepen, and set up a belay.

Climb the tower starting on its right side and working over to the left. A piton is tucked away in a horizontal crack near the start; a few bolts follow, and the pitch is a pumpy struggle to the top. Two-bolt anchor.

review.changed: 3 pitches with grades and lengths (converted from feet). Descent is to rappel the route; no stations listed so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: A short pitch up a one-bolt chimney to a high ledge with the belay anchor.

Start left of the anchor in the corner crack and follow it up and right on gear to the traverse toward the arete. Reach right toward the arete to clip the first of nine bolts; the following 30 ft are thin, reachy and difficult on very small edges. After moving off the arete onto the face the difficulty drops to the anchor that a neighbouring route shares. Either finish over the top, or clip the quick-link and be lowered to the ledge or down to the canyon floor, which a 70 m rope allows.

review.changed: 2 pitches; P2 grade not stated per pitch so left blank.

pitch_detail.notes: Start on a steep but short ice curtain at the base, then a lengthy snow ramp ends at a belay beneath the final steep ice.

Climb a pillar on either the right or left; the right-hand option may offer better rock protection. Pillars can be creaky or worse, so be ready to bail. Finish on an ice slab to a bush or tree anchor. Serious ground with a big penalty for a mistake.

review.changed: 2 pitches with notes only; no per-pitch grades or lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin up a short dihedral to a large ledge, then follow the green and brown patina face toward a left-leaning crack in the middle. From the crack trend up and left toward the left of two green dihedrals and stop on a little grassy ledge under the prominent green corner. Length is about 120 ft. Offsets or totem cams help here.

The best pitch: a well-protected green varnished dihedral about 40 ft long. A questionable block sits to the right at the start, so avoid it. Belay on the ledge made by the right side of the dihedral's end, or link into the next pitch.

From the top of the green corner, follow the obvious crack to a ledge, move left, then a dihedral takes you over the lip to a belay at a tree. About 60 ft. Easily linked with the pitch below using a few long slings.

review.changed: 3 pitches with grades; lengths are approximate in feet so left in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Step left of the neighbouring route's first-pitch corner. Broken cracks and slab lead up, passing two big chicken-head knobs.

pitch_detail.anchor: ledge belay with black totem through .75 cams
pitch_detail.notes: Flared cracks lead to a technical stemming crux; gear improves and rock gets cleaner as it gets harder. A fixed pin helps at the crux. At the top of the corner, a sloping ledge leads left across to the adjacent corner. Belay on a narrow ledge (about 8 inches by 5 ft) using a black totem cam through .75 sized cams; an extra .4 or .5 is nice.

Aid up the beak seam. Bring a handful of #3 beaks, at least one #2 and one #1, a few mostly thick, short Lost Arrows, and extra black totem size cams. Alternatively rappel from the anchor atop a neighbouring route (a 70 m rope barely reaches), or finish up the adjacent corner route.

review.changed: 3 pitches with grades and lengths. Rappel option mentioned but not as a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: The wide crack immediately left of the dihedral leads to a big alcove on the right. Pleasant warm-up with good movement and a roomy belay; avoid the cracks formed by blocks on the ledge when building the anchor.

Exit the alcove over the roof on its right side, using solid underclings and footholds, and continue in a crack that starts at thin hands and widens to size 5. A few chockstones remain in the crack; the belayer is protected in the alcove. Pass a large boulder to a small ledge and belay with smaller gear.
The small ledge leads left back to the dihedral. Put in a .5 cam at waist height, then finish up the corner, which is harder than it appears.

Start up black rock that turns orange, where a boulder-problem crux comes early. Above it a flake takes the rest of the pitch with face and crack climbing, then a few mantles reach the two-bolt anchor on top of a pedestal. The belay can be moved 30 ft to the left, to a large ledge under a small roof, where a bolt sits at head height.
Sustained edge climbing that never gets easier or harder, zigzagging up the face.

Grade is uncertain, around 5.11b. About 35 m or a little more, airy. Go up and right around the roof, clip its bolt, then step left onto the bolt line. The penultimate bolt hides until you step right, when straight up stops looking possible. A last bolt on easy ground precedes a two-bolt anchor on a ledge. To reach the upper headwall, traverse about 50 m up and right along the midway ramp, mindful of loose rock; the next pitch has no anchor at its base.
Grade is uncertain, around 5.11a. An awkward start eases to a rest. After it, unlikely-looking moves go out left, then straight up the face to the belay ledge. Do not give up before the mantle.

Grade is uncertain, around 5.11a. A few moderate bolts lead into the hard moves under the roof, where a high reach is needed. The pitch is steep and feels steeper; keep fighting after the roof. Two-bolt anchor on a comfortable ledge. The summit is about 35 m above via an easy 5th-class dihedral, and the descent walks off west to the saddle.

review.changed: 5 pitches. Uncertain grades kept in notes; P3 length given as 35+ so left in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in a gully and climb mixed ground to the ledge system. Traverse the ledges, which give fun snow climbing, to the last outcrop and build an anchor; cracks hide in the compact rock.
Some more snow to reach the long, low-angle ice ramp with short mixed steps.
Easy snow traverse that leads to the main ice pitch; little real climbing.
The best pitch: a smear of ice that thickens as you climb. A splitter crack low down takes good gear until screws will hold.
A bit of snow, then ice up the narrow gully until it opens out. A fixed anchor on the right wall sits a little higher than expected.

rappel_detail.station: Fixed anchor on the right wall of the upper gully
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel to the snow field above the main ice pitch.

rappel_detail.station: Good tree to the climber's right of the snow field
rappel_detail.notes: Walk right from the snow field and rappel from a solid tree.

review.changed: 5 entries covering 6 pitches (P2 and P3 described together). Rappel table of 2 written from the numbered getting-down list.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble to the steeper slab and clip the first of nine bolts. A cruxy roof comes next, then a bushy ledge and a two-bolt belay.

Bolt-protected featured slab trending left to easier ground, where loose rock may be met, passing three fixed pitons to a good ledge with a two-bolt belay. A solid, juggy flake near the start protects well. A short scramble then reaches the ridge.

review.changed: 2 pitches. Descent is rappel the route; no station list. Care pulling ropes on the upper rappel.

pitch_detail.notes: Find the cracks that lean up and left and follow the parallel finger and fist cracks in the middle until the angle eases and rock quality drops. Belay wherever suits. Afterward, shorten the rope for about 50 m of third class and moderate snow, heading slightly right to a ramp with an obvious tree.
Climb a corner until a little roof forces you left into a second corner, then use turf and front-pointing, and a left horizontal back onto the ridge. Belay on a slung horn.

Keep trending up and left toward dark red rock. A sporty downclimb traverses left under a roof; loose rock, so protect the follower. The belay is on hand-sized gear in a grubby corner under the crux chimney.
Straight up the red chimney from the belay; a #4 cam is useful. Belay on a slung horn, and avoid dropping anything on the belayer.
Follow the ridge on gear or slung belays. Then shorten the rope, cross scree to a moderate snow slope, and go up and left to beneath a large patch of bushes.
Aim for the bushes by the easiest path, then follow a left-trending weakness back to the ridge and continue along it. Gear belay. Above, unrope for third class and gully scrambling to the summit.

review.changed: 6 entries covering 7 pitches (P5 and P6 described together without grades or lengths). Descent by hiking trail or race chutes not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: A short step of about 50 ft to an anchor stance.
Roughly 230 ft of thin climbing in a left-facing corner leads to a rock horn in the gully. The exit is a vertical column that might be detached from the wall; rock gear is available in places there.

review.changed: 2 pitches with lengths converted from feet; no per-pitch grades.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a thin smear of ice and turf, then snow to a large chimney, a first crux: stem, jam and hook up it, then a slab to a belay below a wide crack.
Climb the offwidth to a snow field, then right in the snow to a belay below a slab that leads to a large left-facing corner system.
Steep snow to a slab, then the massive corner, with a tricky overhang; belay above it.
Reach the large ledge just above, walk left to the left-facing corner system, and climb it until rope drag calls for a belay, or use a tree.
Snow and easy mixed ground lead to the trees and the north summit. Rappel the route off blocks and trees, or continue to the main summit.

review.changed: 5 pitches with grades; no lengths given. Rappel via blocks and trees is not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: About 35 m (approximate). Skip the grungy chimney at the back of the alcove; instead climb the hand and fist crack on the alcove's left wall to the first ledge, perhaps 60 ft up. There is an optional mediocre belay here, useful since communication is hard from above. Continue up the leftmost chimney or corner off the ledge, step left onto the face to another hand and fist crack, top out and scamper to a belay at the back of the ledge.
About 25 m (approximate). Choose your own way up a few more steep steps to a big sloping ledge, then work right toward a pair of chimneys; belay beside the left-hand one at a large pillar.

About 30 m (approximate). Scum up the pillar into the chimney, then trend up and right into another one. Where it gets steeper, step onto the face on the right and curl around to a snowy ledge. Belay at the left end of a ledge shared with a neighbouring route about 50 ft right.
About 55 m (approximate). Straight up the gully, then up and left toward the skyline over snow and short mixed steps, to a small conifer just below the ridge top.

review.changed: 4 pitches; lengths stated as approximate so kept in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: About 25 m. An angled ramp, with loose blocks and some moss, leads to a small ledge system; traverse left around the bottom of a steep arete to belay where a chockstone-choked chimney begins.

Stem and squeeze up the chimney to another ledge system with decent protection, surmount a small bulge in a corner, traverse back right toward a right-facing corner and go up it past loose blocks into moderate ground. A huge slung block serves as the belay.
Easy snow and a handful of simple rock steps reach the ridge. The final 200-plus ft were climbed simul.

review.changed: 3 pitches; no grades given. Protection is marginal in places.
